AIArtifactResponse.description:
One answer, plus what it cost to have it.

The generation date is part of the contract and not decoration: on a
manually-refreshed feature it is the only thing telling a reader whether to
ask for a new one.
AIArtifactResponse.title: AIArtifactResponse

AIFeatureFormResponse.description:
What the admin needs to run a feature it was never told about.

The input schema builds the form and the context keys document what the
prompt may refer to. Both are declared on the handler, so a feature added
later gets its screen without a line of frontend.
AIFeatureFormResponse.title: AIFeatureFormResponse

AssetMatch.description: Como o ativo da linha foi achado, ou por que não foi.
AssetMatch.title: AssetMatch

AssetSyncChange.description: Um ativo que o catálogo corrige, com o antes e o depois de cada campo.
AssetSyncChange.title: AssetSyncChange

AssetSyncReport.description: O que a sincronização fez — ou faria, quando `dry_run`.
AssetSyncReport.title: AssetSyncReport

AssetsAndRightsItemResponse.description: Um bem da ficha Bens e Direitos, com os campos na ordem do programa.
AssetsAndRightsItemResponse.title: AssetsAndRightsItemResponse

file.description: Extrato de posição da corretora, em PDF
file.title: File

file.description: Relatório em PDF da carteira recomendada
file.title: File

BrokerageNoteResponse.description: Uma nota importada, para o histórico.
BrokerageNoteResponse.title: BrokerageNoteResponse

CapitalGainOperationResponse.description: Uma alienação de criptoativo para o GCAP.
CapitalGainOperationResponse.title: CapitalGainOperationResponse

ClosedPositionEntry.description:
Um ativo que a carteira teve e não tem mais.

Traz as duas leituras do domínio juntas: o dinheiro realizado na ida e
volta e o retorno ponderado no tempo no último dia de exposição.
ClosedPositionEntry.title: ClosedPositionEntry

ContributionAverage.description:
Quanto entrou por mês, em média, na história inteira da carteira.

Um objeto e não um número solto: a rota responde uma leitura da carteira,
e uma leitura ganha campo com o tempo — um corpo `3909.02` não ganha.

Na moeda pedida na rota, convertido pelo preço do dia da transação, que é
o mesmo critério da série de patrimônio.
ContributionAverage.title: ContributionAverage

CvmRegistrySyncReport.description: O que o sync do cadastro da CVM fez — ou faria, quando `dry_run`.
CvmRegistrySyncReport.title: CvmRegistrySyncReport

DividendKind.description:
O que o provento é para o imposto, e não para a rentabilidade.

Para a carteira os dois são dinheiro que entrou. Para a declaração, o
dividendo é rendimento isento e o JCP é tributado na fonte, em fichas
diferentes — e só o cadastro sabe qual dos dois a empresa pagou.
DividendKind.title: DividendKind

DocumentKind.description: Para que o arquivo foi enviado. O mesmo PDF pode servir aos dois fins.
DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

FIIAllocationResponse.description:
How much of one asset class the fund held.

``value`` is absent for the buildings: the quarterly filing counts and
describes them, but declares no price for them.
FIIAllocationResponse.title: FIIAllocationResponse

FIICompositionPointResponse.description: One quarter of the composition history: the totals, not the items.
FIICompositionPointResponse.title: FIICompositionPointResponse

FIICompositionResponse.description: What the fund held at the end of the last quarter it filed for.
FIICompositionResponse.title: FIICompositionResponse

FIIDividendResponse.description:
One payment per share, as published.

``event_type`` is what the fund called it — an ordinary distribution or an
amortization of capital. It is carried so that a reader meaning income can
tell the two apart instead of adding them up.
FIIDividendResponse.title: FIIDividendResponse

FIIHoldingResponse.description: One financial asset the fund holds: a CRI, a share in another fund.
FIIHoldingResponse.title: FIIHoldingResponse

FIIIndicatorsResponse.description:
The fund's own numbers, as of the report they came from.

The yields and the monthly return are ratios: 0.12381 is 12.381%.
``price_to_nav`` is the published P/VP, a multiple around 1. None of them
is scaled here; the client decides how each is written.
FIIIndicatorsResponse.title: FIIIndicatorsResponse

FIIManagementResponse.description: Who runs the fund and under which mandate.
FIIManagementResponse.title: FIIManagementResponse

FIIMonthlyReportResponse.description:
The monthly filing: what the fund's equity is made of, in reais.

The rates are ratios like everywhere else here, and the monetary fields are
absolute amounts, not per share. Indicators the filing repeats are served by
``FIIIndicatorsResponse`` instead of being restated under a second name.
FIIMonthlyReportResponse.title: FIIMonthlyReportResponse

FIIProfileResponse.description:
Everything the fund publishes about itself.

Every section is optional and independent: the provider answers each from a
route of its own, and one of them failing costs the page that section
rather than the whole profile. The monthly sections and the quarterly ones
also carry different dates, which is why each states its own.
FIIProfileResponse.title: FIIProfileResponse

FIIPropertyResponse.description: One building, as the fund described it in the quarterly filing.
FIIPropertyResponse.title: FIIPropertyResponse

FIIPropertySummaryResponse.description:
The fund's buildings added up, as of one quarter.

``vacancy_rate`` is consolidated and ``average_vacancy_rate`` is the plain
average across buildings; areas are in square metres.
FIIPropertySummaryResponse.title: FIIPropertySummaryResponse

FavoriteAsset.description: An asset the user returns to, ranked by how often they open it.
FavoriteAsset.title: FavoriteAsset

ForeignItemResponse.description: O rendimento de um bem no exterior no ano, com de onde ele vem.
ForeignItemResponse.title: ForeignItemResponse

ForeignYearResponse.description: A apuração anual do exterior: a conta que o programa refaz, para conferir.
ForeignYearResponse.title: ForeignYearResponse

Frequency-Input.description:
Com que passo uma coisa se repete ao longo da simulação.

Aporte e rebalanceamento andam no mesmo calendário — de mês em mês, de
trimestre em trimestre —, então são a mesma enumeração e não duas iguais.
`NONE` é a ausência do regime, e significa coisas diferentes em cada um:
sem aporte, só o valor inicial trabalha; sem rebalanceamento, quem corrige
a carteira são os aportes.
Frequency-Input.title: Frequency

FundLinkSuggestionReport.description:
As propostas de vínculo entre um FII e o fundo que o regulador registrou.

`ambiguous` é um CNPJ que aponta para mais de um registro e `unknown` é um
que o registro não conhece. Nenhum dos dois vira palpite.
FundLinkSuggestionReport.title: FundLinkSuggestionReport

FundSeriesFilingOut.description:
The latest FIDC filing of a class. ``applicable`` is false for classes
that do not file by series; ``filing_date`` is null when no file listed by
the source has a filing for the class.
FundSeriesFilingOut.title: FundSeriesFilingOut

HistoricalCagrResponse.description: Annualized growth over the served history, and the window it covers.
HistoricalCagrResponse.title: HistoricalCagrResponse

ImportRequest.description: Uma nota por vez: o cabeçalho que será gravado, as linhas e as decisões.
ImportRequest.title: ImportRequest

IncomeLineResponse.description: Uma linha de Rendimentos Isentos ou de Tributação Exclusiva.
IncomeLineResponse.title: IncomeLineResponse

InstitutionOut.description: Uma pessoa jurídica: companhia emissora, administradora, gestora.
InstitutionOut.title: InstitutionOut

InvestmentFundDividendResponse.description:
One payment per share, as published.

``event_type`` is what the fund called it — an ordinary distribution or an
amortization of capital. It is carried so that a reader meaning income can
tell the two apart instead of adding them up.

The provider does not estimate a payment date from a fixed interval, since
funds of these kinds have none, so no periodicity may be read into the
series either.
InvestmentFundDividendResponse.title: InvestmentFundDividendResponse

InvestmentFundHoldingResponse.description:
One line of the quarterly portfolio filing.

``bucket`` says which group the line came from — ``public_bonds``,
``fund_holdings``, ``credit_assets``, ``listed_securities``, ``receivables``
or ``payables``. The last two are claims and obligations rather than things
owned, which is why the group travels with the line: added up blindly, a
payable would inflate what the fund holds.

``details`` is whatever else the filing said. Its keys vary by group and by
fund, so it is served as filed rather than promoted into fields that would
be absent for most rows.
InvestmentFundHoldingResponse.title: InvestmentFundHoldingResponse

InvestmentFundIdentityResponse.description:
What the fund is, on paper: its registration and who runs it.

``kind`` is the family the fund belongs to — ``fiagro``, ``fidc``,
``fiinfra``, ``fif``, ``fip`` — and it decides what the rest of the profile
can contain: a FIDC files monthly share values and no daily ones, a FIP
files neither. The three classifications come from three different bodies
and disagree on purpose, so none stands for the others.
InvestmentFundIdentityResponse.title: InvestmentFundIdentityResponse

InvestmentFundIndicatorsResponse.description:
The fund's own numbers, as of the filing they came from.

The returns and the yield are ratios: 0.0142 is 1.42%. ``price_to_nav`` is
the published P/VP, a multiple around 1 — below it the share trades for less
than the fund says it is worth. None of them is scaled here; the client
decides how each is written.

``daily_applications`` and ``daily_redemptions`` are the money that came in
and went out on the reference day, in reais. A closed-end fund files zero
for both because nobody can subscribe or redeem.
InvestmentFundIndicatorsResponse.title: InvestmentFundIndicatorsResponse

InvestmentFundInvestorBreakdownResponse.description:
Who holds the fund, in the monthly filing.

Counts and shares are both served: one feeder fund is one investor and the
whole of the equity, and either number alone tells half of that.
InvestmentFundInvestorBreakdownResponse.title: InvestmentFundInvestorBreakdownResponse

InvestmentFundMarketFundResponse.description:
One fund in the catalogue, summarized.

``asset_id`` is filled only for funds registered in the application, and it
is what makes a row open a page — the rest of the catalogue is readable but
has nothing to open.
InvestmentFundMarketFundResponse.title: InvestmentFundMarketFundResponse

InvestmentFundNavPointResponse.description:
One filing of the share value, with the equity behind it.

It is the fund's own accounting and not its market price: a share that has
not traded in a week still has a share value filed every day. A FIDC files
per class or series, so ``class_or_series`` is part of what identifies a row.
InvestmentFundNavPointResponse.title: InvestmentFundNavPointResponse

InvestmentFundPortfolioResponse.description: What the fund held at the end of the last quarter it filed for.
InvestmentFundPortfolioResponse.title: InvestmentFundPortfolioResponse

InvestmentFundPortfolioSummaryResponse.description:
The quarterly filing added up, by group.

``market_value`` is the filing's own total and is not the sum of the six
groups below it: receivables add to it and payables subtract from it.
InvestmentFundPortfolioSummaryResponse.title: InvestmentFundPortfolioSummaryResponse

InvestmentFundProfileResponse.description:
Everything the fund publishes about itself.

Every section is optional and independent: the provider answers each from a
route of its own, and one of them failing costs the page that section rather
than the whole profile. The sections also arrive on different clocks — the
share value daily or monthly, the regulatory profile monthly, the portfolio
quarterly and months late — which is why each states its own date.
InvestmentFundProfileResponse.title: InvestmentFundProfileResponse

InvestmentFundRegulatoryProfileResponse.description:
The most recent monthly filing with the regulator.

Only the funds the regulator asks it of file one, so an absent profile is a
fact about the fund's kind rather than a failure to read it.
InvestmentFundRegulatoryProfileResponse.title: InvestmentFundRegulatoryProfileResponse

InvestmentFundRiskResponse.description:
How the fund measures its own risk, in the monthly filing.

``risk_model`` is what makes the numbers beside it comparable or not: a VaR
from a non-parametric model and one from a parametric model are not the same
quantity, so the model travels with them.
InvestmentFundRiskResponse.title: InvestmentFundRiskResponse

LastRunResponse.description: The last run of a routine: its task run, what it sent, its execution.
LastRunResponse.title: LastRunResponse

LevelReadingResponse.description:
A level against its own weekly history. Returns and distances are
fractions; percentiles run from 0 to 1.
LevelReadingResponse.title: LevelReadingResponse

ManualStart.description: How a person starts the routine.
ManualStart.title: ManualStart

MarketDataSeriesOption.description: Minimal identity used to pick a series in a selector.
MarketDataSeriesOption.title: MarketDataSeriesOption

MarketDataSeriesResponse.description: A registered series with everything that identifies and types it.
MarketDataSeriesResponse.title: MarketDataSeriesResponse

MarketDataSeriesTimeSeries.description: Each series by its short name, mapped to its observations.
MarketDataSeriesTimeSeries.title: MarketDataSeriesTimeSeries

NoteAmountsSchema.description: Totais, custos e líquido como a nota os imprime; os custos, positivos.
NoteAmountsSchema.title: NoteAmountsSchema

NoteLineRequest.description: Uma linha como a pessoa a conferiu: o ativo e a corretora já escolhidos, ou não.
NoteLineRequest.title: NoteLineRequest

PortfolioConsolidation.description:
When the portfolio's derived data was last rebuilt.

`consolidated_at` is when the run finished, not the date the numbers reach:
that one is bounded by the last quote ingested.
PortfolioConsolidation.title: PortfolioConsolidation

PortfolioDocumentResponse.description: Um arquivo enviado à carteira, para o histórico.
PortfolioDocumentResponse.title: PortfolioDocumentResponse

PortfolioSummary.description: Portfolio identity without its categories, for administrative listings.
PortfolioSummary.title: PortfolioSummary

PortfolioWealthTier.description:
A portfolio's standing on the ladder, as it is today.

`current_patrimony` decides everything: `current_tier`, `remaining` and
`progress` all falam do valor de hoje, e a patente desce quando a carteira
desce.

`peak_patrimony` é o mais alto que a carteira já valeu. Ele é história,
e não decide o título.
PortfolioWealthTier.title: PortfolioWealthTier

RateReadingResponse.description: A rate, as a fraction per year, against its own weekly history.
RateReadingResponse.title: RateReadingResponse

RecommendationChange.description:
What an edition did with a line, compared to the previous one.

`UNCHANGED` and an absent change are different statements: the first is the
report saying it kept the position, the second is the report not saying
anything, which is what most of them do for most lines.
RecommendationChange.title: RecommendationChange

RecommendationConsensusResponse.description: O ranking mais o que ficou de fora dele.
RecommendationConsensusResponse.title: RecommendationConsensusResponse

RecommendedPortfolioDraftResponse.description: The reading of one PDF, for the screen that shows it before it is kept.
RecommendedPortfolioDraftResponse.title: RecommendedPortfolioDraftResponse

ReferenceEtfReadingResponse.title: ReferenceEtfReadingResponse

RegisteredFundOut.description: Um fundo do cadastro do regulador, como a busca manual o devolve.
RegisteredFundOut.title: RegisteredFundOut

RegistrySyncFieldChange.description: O antes e o depois de um campo que o regulador corrige.
RegistrySyncFieldChange.title: RegistrySyncFieldChange

RunBacktestRequest.description:
Uma simulação pedida.

A alocação vem inteira no corpo, e não como o id de uma carteira salva: é o
que deixa a tela simular um rascunho que ninguém salvou, e o que faz o
comparador e o painel de variações usarem a mesma rota.
RunBacktestRequest.title: RunBacktestRequest

StockCashDividendResponse.description:
A payment in money, per share.

``label`` tells a dividend from interest on own capital (``JCP``), which is
taxed at source. ``last_date_prior`` is the last day the share carried the
right; the ex date is the trading day after. ``payment_date`` is regularly
in the future, because a company announces months ahead.
StockCashDividendResponse.title: StockCashDividendResponse

StockCompanyResponse.description:
The business behind the ticker.

The classification comes twice: ``sector``/``industry`` are for reading and
``sector_key``/``industry_key`` are stable slugs meant for grouping. The
summary arrives already split into the paragraphs the company wrote.
StockCompanyResponse.title: StockCompanyResponse

StockFundamentalsResponse.description:
How the business did, before the market had an opinion.

Margins, returns and growth are ratios. ``earnings_growth`` and
``revenue_growth`` compare a quarter to the same quarter a year earlier;
the ``annual_`` pair compares years, and the two are far apart enough that
a screen has to say which it is showing.
StockFundamentalsResponse.title: StockFundamentalsResponse

StockPriceRangeResponse.description:
The quote and the band the year drew around it.

``day_change`` is a ratio like every other proportion here: 0.0199 is
+1,99%. The provider states this one in percentage points and it is divided
on the way in, so that nothing downstream has to know which route wrote it.
StockPriceRangeResponse.title: StockPriceRangeResponse

StockProfileResponse.description:
Everything a listed company publishes about itself.

Every section is optional and independent: the provider answers each from a
route of its own, and one of them failing costs the page that section rather
than the whole profile. The series run oldest first.

``ticker`` is what was asked for and ``resolved_ticker`` is what the market
calls it now; ``renamed`` says the two differ, so a reader who lands on a
page under an unfamiliar code is told why.
StockProfileResponse.title: StockProfileResponse

StockShareDividendResponse.description:
A payment in shares: a bonus issue or a split.

It has a proportion and no amount, and never had a payment date -- which is
why it is its own shape rather than a cash dividend with half its fields
empty.
StockShareDividendResponse.title: StockShareDividendResponse

StockStatementPointResponse.description:
One period of one filed statement, carrying only the lines it has.

``lines`` is a mapping and not a set of fields because the filers disagree
on which lines exist: the provider answers each statement with every line
any Brazilian filer might report -- 128 for the balance sheet -- and a bank
fills a different 31 of them than an oil company fills 65, with 16 in
common. Declared as fields, three quarters of the contract would be null for
any one company. Keys are the provider's line names in snake_case, and a
line the company did not file is absent rather than zero.

``period`` is what the filer called it -- ``quarterly``, ``yearly`` --
echoed rather than normalized.
StockStatementPointResponse.title: StockStatementPointResponse

StockStatisticsResponse.description:
What the market pays for the company.

The multiples are as the provider publishes them and are never recomputed
from price and earnings. ``dividend_yield``, ``profit_margin`` and
``fifty_two_week_change`` are ratios: 0.08 is 8%.
StockStatisticsResponse.title: StockStatisticsResponse

StockSubscriptionResponse.description: A right to subscribe new shares, which is neither of the other two.
StockSubscriptionResponse.title: StockSubscriptionResponse

UpdateRecommendedPortfolioRequest.description: O que uma carteira já salva aceita mudar depois da importação.
UpdateRecommendedPortfolioRequest.title: UpdateRecommendedPortfolioRequest

WealthTier.description: Um degrau da escala: um título e o preço dele.
WealthTier.title: WealthTier

WealthTierProjection.description:
Quando o degrau seguinte chega, no ritmo atual.

As duas entradas viajam junto com a resposta porque a data sozinha não se
defende: ela vale o que valem o aporte médio e a taxa que a produziram.
WealthTierProjection.title: WealthTierProjection

`NONE` é a ausência do regime, e significa coisas diferentes em cada um:

app__modules__lab__domain__enums__Freque.title: Frequency

app__modules__research__domain__draft__P.description:
Whether the ticker a report names is one the catalogue carries.

Three answers and not two: a ticker registered twice — the same code under
two asset types — is not the same problem as one that is missing, and the
screen resolves them differently. Guessing between two candidates here
would link a recommendation to the wrong asset without saying so.
app__modules__research__domain__draft__P.title: PositionMatch

get.description:
O rascunho do texto de cadastro, para o botão de preencher.

Lê o que já existe e só gera quando não há nada — clicar duas vezes não
paga duas vezes. Querer um rascunho diferente é uma decisão, e ela entra
pela rota de execução.

Nada daqui chega ao cadastro: o texto vai para o formulário, e o que fica
gravado em `asset.summary` e `asset.description` é o que o mantenedor
salvar.

post.description:
Confirma o vínculo de um FII ou ETF com um fundo do registro.

É por aqui que o ETF entra: o catálogo do provedor não traz o CNPJ dele,
então o fundo é achado pela busca do registro e confirmado à mão.

get.description:
As propostas de vínculo entre um FII e o fundo registrado na CVM.

Só propõe: um CNPJ que aponta para mais de um registro sai como ambíguo, e
um que o registro não conhece sai como desconhecido. Nenhum dos dois vira
palpite, e nada é gravado aqui.

post.description:
Casar o cadastro local com o que a CVM publica sobre companhias.

Preenche as pessoas jurídicas e liga cada ação à companhia que a emitiu,
com a espécie do papel e o segmento de listagem que vêm junto. `dry_run` é
o padrão porque a rota reescreve dado que a tela mostra: primeiro se lê o
relatório, depois se repete com `dry_run=false`.

Casar o cadastro local com o catálogo do provedor.

Nomes e logos vêm do provedor, tickers que faltam viram ativos novos, e o
que só existe aqui continua existindo. `dry_run` é o padrão porque a rota
reescreve dado que a tela mostra: primeiro se olha o relatório, depois se
repete com `dry_run=false`.
